correctness.rationale: The exact polynomial formulas for n=3t+r exhibit a bijective branch g2(t)=t+3A(t). Branches g0/3 and g1/3 reduce to opposite t(t-1) modulo 3, so Hensel supplies unique simple critical points; their Taylor expansions are globally conjugate to signed squares by 3-adic isometries. Counting square roots and the three lifts in each ramified branch proves N_k(y) for all k, then singleton counts and maxima follow. Vandermonde proves the 3^(k+1) period and the g2 isometry proves it minimal. Packaged verify.py independently checks all 88,572 target fibers through k=10, 265,716 indices, and root/singleton/max formulas. Finite tests do not replace the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Existing binomial theorems already establish the least period and surjectivity but do not evaluate how many indices represent every target modulo each 3^k. Searches for fifth-column ternary fibers and aliases found no dominating theorem. The same-column exact published theorem is specifically dyadic; the closest ternary result treats the sixth binomial column image, not fifth-column fibers. Checked accessible current-week claim records for deduplication; earlier-week history is incompletely accessible. An unindexed equivalence remains a genuine bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent fifth-column ternary fiber classification may predate this result.
The wider literature beyond the identified primary sources and relevant accessible research entries was not exhaustively screened.
The 3-adic critical values lack simple rational closed forms; Hensel lifting is required for evaluation.
Finite verification is limited to k<=10; unrestricted correctness relies on the algebraic conjugacy proof.

value.rationale: Among residues already known to be attained by binom(n,5), the full target multiplicity is a natural nontrivial distributional invariant. The explicit two quadratic critical shells give a complete all-level classification, a sharp two-target maximum for every k>=4, and the exact limiting singleton-target fraction 31/36. These quantify naturally motivated collision and uniqueness phenomena not answered by density of the image alone. This is an infinite structural classification, not a finite enumerative slice.
